chunks: Position and velocity from accelerometer. The question: How can you determine position/velocity from the accelerometer data?
Velocity is how fast you are going, and position is where you are. If you know acceleration over time, you can add it up to get velocity, and add velocity up to get position.
It works on paper, but small errors in the readings grow very fast, so in practice it only holds for a few seconds.
Picture a jar that gets one stray coin every second, by mistake. Its count grows steadily: 1, 2, 3, 4.
Every second you also add that jar's count to a second jar, which then holds 1, 3, 6, 10. The first jar is the velocity error and the second is the position error.
A tiny mistake, added up twice, grows faster and faster.
Log scale, so power-law growth appears as gentle curves. Every consumer-grade error crosses the 1 m line within about 5 to 15 seconds.
Only navigation-grade accuracy (1 µg, green) stays below a few centimetres over a minute. Doubling the time quadruples the error.
Integrate: add up a quantity over time. Acceleration integrates to velocity, and velocity integrates to position.
Bias: a small constant error in a sensor's output, even when the true input is zero. Drift: an error that keeps growing as time passes.
Gravity: an accelerometer feels it too, so it must be subtracted out or it looks like real motion.
Dead reckoning: finding position by adding up motion from a known starting point.
Lay the device perfectly still, but say its accelerometer has a bias of 0. 02 m/s². After 10 seconds, the false velocity is 0. 02 times 10 = 0. 2 m/s.
The false position is half of 0. 02 times 10 squared, which is 1 m. Wait 20 seconds and it is 4 m: double the time, four times the error.
If we forgot gravity, the false acceleration would be 9. 81 m/s², about 490 m of fake travel in 10 seconds.
"You integrate acceleration once for velocity and again for position, after removing gravity using the orientation.
But bias integrates twice: a bias b gives position error b t squared over two, so 1 milli-g is about 18 metres after a minute.
Tilt error leaks gravity into the horizontal axes, and 0. 1 degrees is about 31 metres per minute.
So with a consumer IMU it only works for seconds, unless you reset velocity with zero-velocity updates or fuse with GPS, vision or odometry."
Quick check. Why can't you just integrate raw accelerometer readings twice to get position?
